rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout (pre-existing from iter-12): server.py _check_brute_force uses `identifier = f"{request.client.host}:{email}"`. In Kubernetes behind the ingress proxy, `request.client.host` resolves to the last-hop pod IP, which varies across requests hitting different pods. 6 failed logins therefore split across multiple counters (e.g., 10.79.131.66 has 3, 10.79.131.71 has 3), neither ever reaches the 5-fail threshold, so 401 is returned forever instead of 429. Mitigation: read X-Forwarded-For first entry (or the X-Real-IP header) and use only that + email as the identifier; or drop IP entirely and rate-limit per-email (with risk of DoS-via-valid-email — mitigable by a short TTL lockout).
